RagShortTexts: The standing military of Goths in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Goths rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Goths against overwhelming regional adversaries.

At the bronze horn's call, spearmen step into place with shields overlapped edge to edge. Mounted attackers crash against the front rank while the second rank thrusts through the gaps. Whoever breaks the line to run is cut down by his own file, since retreat without an order is death.

A grey-bearded commander studies the field from a wagon bed, comparing the ranks with the list of levies he summoned. Battles like this are won in the supply tent before the first arrow flies: grain must arrive on time and the line must hold straight. Once the enemy center gives way, the riders are ordered forward to close the gap.
